question: Which of the following languages had a negative decadal (2001-11) growth rate (its speakers) according to Census of India, 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Urdu__.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urdu had a negative decadal (2001-11) growth rate (its speakers) according to the Census of India, 2011.**
 
• **As per the language census data 2011:**
 
 
• Two scheduled languages, **Urdu and Konkani, saw a fall in absolute numbers.**
 
• There are 50772631 Urdu speakers in India, **a fall of about 1.5 percent since 2001.**
 
• The **decline in Konkani speakers is 9.5 percent.**
 
• The **Urdu language in modern India is associated only with Muslims.**
 
• This **fall in Urdu speakers is strange as the Muslim population in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar has grown between 2001 and 2011.​ [IMAGE: file:///C:/Users/akhil/Desktop/22languagelist.jpg] [IMAGE: file:///C:/Users/akhil/Desktop/22languagelist.jpg] **
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Office of the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India June 26, 2018,** **released the 2011 Census data on Language and Mother Tongue. **
 
• **Key Highlights of the 2011 Census data on Language and Mother Tongue**
 
 
• As per the 2011 census, **43.63 percent of Indians speak Hindi** as their mother tongue.
 
• **Bengali, with 8.03 percent speakers, is second on the list.**
 
• Marathi at 3rd with 6.86 percent speakers, Telugu at 4th with 6.7 percent speakers, and Tamil at 5th with 5.7 percent speakers.
 
• In all, **13 of the 22 scheduled languages** were reported as the** mother tongue by at least 1 percent of the population.**
 
• **Except for Sanskrit,** **each of the 21 scheduled languages** was reported as the **mother tongue by at least 10 lakh people.**
 
• Sanskrit is the only language that is spoken by a set of around 25000 people.
